7.1.decision: Use as a self-check and a source of topic gaps. Review quiz explanations critically; this audit does not establish credential recognition or hiring value.

courses.title: LiveKit Architecture

chapters.title: Why WebRTC? The latency problem in voice AI
chapters.assessment: The transport motivation is useful: media deadlines, congestion and ordered TCP recovery can change conversational latency. The book already explains those mechanisms more carefully. The lesson turns that motivation into universal transport and latency rankings, which should not become interview facts. An optional link can connect the packet deadline explanation to measured speech-end-to-playout latency; no new generic WebRTC question is needed.

chapters.title: P2P vs MCU vs SFU: why LiveKit chose the SFU
chapters.assessment: Mesh, mixing and selective forwarding are useful comparison axes. The book already covers bandwidth and subscriber costs. The lesson overgeneralizes room scaling and treats one distributed self-hosted room as if participants were automatically spread across SFUs. A short self-hosted room-placement versus Cloud architecture note would add precision; participant limits require a declared workload.

chapters.title: Rooms, Participants & Tracks: universal primitives
chapters.assessment: The room/participant/publication/subscription vocabulary is helpful interview preparation and already present. Some properties are simplified too aggressively: metadata is not uniformly a key/value store, permissions still constrain participants, and a room is more than a cost-free routing entry. Optionally add a small vocabulary table separating identity, permission, participant attributes and room metadata.

chapters.title: AI agents as room participants
chapters.assessment: The shared media participant model explains why browsers, SIP endpoints and agents interoperate. It does not eliminate the AgentServer, job dispatch, process lifecycle or provider connections. The book already draws this runtime distinction. Use the lesson as an introductory mental model, followed immediately by LK-02 for dispatch and ownership.

chapters.title: The data plane: streams, RPC & state sync
chapters.assessment: Text/byte streams, RPC and synchronized state are useful separate communication patterns. Their live delivery semantics do not supply durable request identity or business transactions. The book already has the stronger P2 inbox comparison. Add metadata-versus-attributes and RPC timeout ambiguity as brief RTC-06 follow-ups rather than another durability chapter.

chapters.title: Extending the room: telephony, egress & ingress
chapters.assessment: Ingress imports external media; egress exports or records; SIP bridges phone participants. This gives useful product vocabulary beyond the book’s native browser and signed SMS simulation. These services have independent deployment, credentials, capacity and evidence requirements. Recommend an architecture boundary glossary only, coordinated with the separate phones course review. Do not imply that this POC implemented or qualified SIP, ingress or egress.

chapters.title: Security, encryption & self-hosting
chapters.assessment: The encryption layering and self-hosting discussion belongs with the existing trust-boundary question. Key distribution is an application responsibility, and an agent that consumes clear media must be an authorized decrypting endpoint. E2EE does not hide signaling/API metadata. Tighten the key-distribution and agent-endpoint explanation if the book is later revised; do not copy unverified automatic key-negotiation claims.

chapters.title: The universal SDK ecosystem
chapters.assessment: Client, server and Agents SDKs solve different jobs, which is directly relevant to the role. The broad platform catalogue is orientation, not a feature-parity guarantee. Platform support and plugin availability must be checked against a chosen release. Add a three-tier SDK comparison to ROLE-08, grounded in token issuance, room transport and agent runtime responsibilities.

courses.decision: Use as an architecture refresher. Existing WebRTC and authority chapters already cover most of it; qualify universal latency, topology and SDK-parity claims.
courses.treatment: Link existing RTC-01 to RTC-08 and LK-01/LK-02; add a small SDK-family and state-lifetime table.
courses.review_summary: Transport and room vocabulary are useful, but the book already supplies stronger durability, trust and measurement boundaries. Recommended additions are a short SDK-tier glossary and a self-hosted room-placement note.

courses.title: Competitive Landscape

chapters.title: LiveKit Agents vs Pipecat
chapters.assessment: The useful comparison is integrated room transport and agent runtime versus an explicitly assembled media-processing pipeline. Claims about a competitor’s missing interruption, state, deployment or UI features need release-specific primary evidence, which this chapter does not supply. Retain the build-versus-compose discussion; avoid copying superiority tables, download counts, unsupported accuracy rankings or feature absence claims.

chapters.title: LiveKit vs managed platforms
chapters.assessment: Control over code, transport, deployment and debugging is a useful build/buy framework. The lesson mixes that framework with volatile prices, fixed added latency and platform/compliance assertions. Those figures are not qualified evidence for this application. Compare ownership, observability, portability, residency requirements and integration cost using current primary documentation before making a real purchase decision.

chapters.title: Choosing your approach
chapters.assessment: The five decision dimensions are useful, but fixed volume thresholds cannot prove a framework is cheaper or a managed service is suitable. Migration also includes tool schemas, event semantics, media behavior, testing and operational changes, not only prompt transfer. An optional interview exercise can ask for a neutral requirements matrix and measured total cost; the current book already supports this product judgment.

courses.decision: Keep the build-versus-buy reasoning. Competitor features, pricing and comparative superiority need dated primary evidence.
courses.treatment: Add a decision rubric to SDK/product discussion, without a frozen vendor ranking or pricing table.
courses.review_summary: A neutral ownership/control/operability comparison is useful. Commercial prices, compliance claims and competitor absence statements should not be reproduced as established facts. No new full question is justified beyond the existing product-judgment coverage.

courses.title: Voice AI Foundations

chapters.title: What is voice AI? Why WebRTC matters
chapters.assessment: The beginner pipeline and conversation-loop framing is already covered. Separate transport latency, endpointing, inference, synthesis and playout rather than repeating universal subsecond thresholds or treating WebRTC as the only possible voice transport. No new question; direct readers to LK-03 and the existing latency diagnosis.

chapters.title: Project setup & your first agent
chapters.assessment: Installing dependencies, selecting providers and starting a local agent is useful practice. The displayed Python entrypoint receives an AgentSession and passes models to start; pinned 1.8.11 instead supplies JobContext and configures the session or agent models before start. A later supplement should show a minimal pinned-version setup and explain which component owns each resource. Examples were reviewed statically, not installed or run.

chapters.title: Understanding AgentSession
chapters.assessment: AgentSession coordinates I/O, active-agent behavior and model components. That orchestration does not remove application responsibility for external clients, background tasks or shutdown. Several symbols and event-handler shapes in the lesson need release verification. An SDK lifecycle note would complement the project’s deeper ownership examples without claiming automatic resource safety.

chapters.title: Writing great agent instructions
chapters.assessment: Specific role, tone, boundaries, examples and concise spoken replies are useful prompt-design topics. They are behavior guidance, not enforcement of mutation authority or external truth. The lesson’s shared startup scaffold has the same pinned-version defects as project setup. Recommend a compact contrast between good voice instructions and independently enforced tool policy; avoid another broad security question.

chapters.title: Adding your first tool: check availability
chapters.assessment: Function-tool schemas and concise model-facing results are useful SDK basics. RunContext injection is not a universal positional-first requirement, and schema conformity cannot authorize a booking or validate the business meaning of a date. Tie schema-derived tool arguments to P1’s independently validated public command rather than presenting the tool decorator as the business boundary.

chapters.title: RunContext, state & the booking tool
chapters.assessment: This is a readable demonstration of contextual session state and expected ToolError responses. The appointment is stored in memory and announced by speech, so it is not evidence of durable booking, an idempotent supplier operation or exact human confirmation. A useful exercise compares this toy booking with P1’s separate confirmation, intent, effect and receipt. Do not translate an unknown database/supplier outcome into a definitive failure.

chapters.title: Noise cancellation & room configuration
chapters.assessment: Room input and noise processing introduce a worthwhile audio path. Noise reduction, acoustic echo cancellation, background voice cancellation and VAD solve different problems. Provider/platform availability and extra latency should be checked for the actual plugin and environment. Add a diagnostic diagram showing capture, echo/noise processing, VAD/STT and output; avoid fixed processing budgets presented as guarantees.

chapters.title: Testing your agent
chapters.assessment: Turn-level agent tests and semantic judges are a real gap in the book’s SDK coverage. The lesson’s claimed lack of network is contradicted by provider-backed generation and judging. Its examples also require correction to the pinned AgentSession/RunResult contract. Propose REC-P1-08: deterministic tool assertions, model-behavior evaluation and actual audio tests establish different facts.

chapters.title: Turn detection deep dive
chapters.assessment: Endpointing and backchannel quality are useful, but the text MultilingualModel is conflated with adaptive audio interruption detection. The flattened configuration examples do not match the pinned nested TurnHandlingOptions structure. Propose REC-P1-03/04, separating speech activity, text end-of-turn, interruption onset and false-interruption recovery.

chapters.title: Conversation context & multi-turn state
chapters.assessment: Preserving useful context while bounding history is worth teaching. The SDK history is heterogeneous; a messages-only slice can damage tool-call relationships. Backend token or room metadata does not automatically hydrate trusted AgentSession.userdata. Propose REC-P1-02, connecting explicit scoped hydration and valid context truncation to the existing P2 read-only rehydration contract.

chapters.title: Beyond audio: the data plane
chapters.assessment: Rich text, JSON bytes and attributes demonstrate live agent/UI interaction. Publishing a confirmation does not prove a retained input, completed business operation or rendered user output. Room access in these examples must be taken from the real job/runtime contract. The book already distinguishes transport, durable intake and playback; optionally add a metadata/attribute example after API correction.

chapters.title: Deploy to LiveKit Cloud
chapters.assessment: Deployment steps are orientation, not evidence that the application is secure, drained safely or qualified for provider/media behavior. The book’s local-only target means Cloud deployment is an optional learning exercise, not a missing completion prerequisite. Recommend a pinned, separate deployment exercise only if desired; do not copy floating dependency ranges or claim it ran.

chapters.title: Polish & production readiness
chapters.assessment: Greeting, silence handling and background audio are useful UX topics after correctness. The assembled toy still inherits startup/turn API defects and in-memory booking limitations. A no-interruption utterance does not establish that a user heard or consented to it. Prioritize measured interaction quality and lifecycle ownership before background-audio polish; inspect current player start/close APIs before using the sample.

courses.decision: Read for framework vocabulary and lifecycle. Your existing project is beyond the starter application; several examples need API verification.
courses.treatment: Extract tools, context and lifecycle questions. Keep a beginner setup route as a reference rather than another long implementation chapter.
courses.review_summary: The real gaps are framework lifecycle/state, conversation evaluations and exact turn semantics. The in-memory booking example is a useful contrast with P1, not evidence that SDK tools create durable business transactions.

courses.title: Agent Frontends

chapters.title: Frontend architecture for the dental receptionist
chapters.assessment: The room/participant/track mental model is already covered. Keep the browser-to-agent architecture as a teaching example, distinguishing media tracks from higher-level text/data APIs.

chapters.title: Connecting to the dental receptionist
chapters.assessment: Add a frontend token-minting threat model. The lesson keeps secrets server-side but its GET example does not authenticate the application user; caller-supplied labels cannot establish room/account authorization.

chapters.title: Agent dispatch
chapters.assessment: Expand explicit versus automatic dispatch, room-creation-only token configuration and validated dispatch metadata. Dispatch success still precedes agent connection, media and application readiness.

chapters.title: Agent state & the dental session lifecycle
chapters.assessment: Separate transport connection, SDK agent state and business status. The lesson's six-state universal agent machine differs from the pinned SDK's AgentState literal; disconnected UI does not establish booking failure.

chapters.title: Transcription & booking confirmations
chapters.assessment: Add streaming transcript reconciliation and recovery of missed confirmation cards. A live topic or participant attribute is a projection; the backend receipt remains the source for confirmed business outcomes.

chapters.title: Text input for the dental receptionist
chapters.assessment: The book already explains typed input, STT bypass and durable intake. Retain voice/text coexistence while avoiding the claim that typed input must always produce TTS or use the POC's opt-in intake adapter.

chapters.title: RPC & data channels: a visual booking flow
chapters.assessment: Add authenticated RPC design and mechanism selection: RPC for bounded responses, attributes for low-frequency state and streams for text/bytes. Correct the lesson's AgentSession RPC event registration and preserve durable mutation identities.

courses.decision: A strong source of missing frontend questions: token authorization, dispatch readiness and the different data APIs.
courses.treatment: Add token-minting and RPC/stream/state scenarios, with durable business authority kept separate from realtime convenience APIs.
courses.review_summary: Recommend a focused frontend/API expansion: secure token issuance, explicit dispatch and RPC/state/stream semantics. Most room, durable-text and reconnect material is already present.

courses.title: Connect to the Phone Network

chapters.title: How telephony works in LiveKit
chapters.assessment: Add the SIP-signaling/RTP-media bridge and independent evidence for trunk arrival, room placement and agent readiness. Phone participants expose useful attributes but are not interchangeable with browser identities for authorization.

chapters.title: Buy a number & configure inbound trunk
chapters.assessment: Keep provider provisioning as optional lab references. Number availability, provider credentials and regional restrictions need current provider documentation; buying a number is not central to the Agents SDK interview.

chapters.title: Dispatch rules: routing calls to agents
chapters.assessment: This is a material conceptual correction: room_prefix names SIP rooms; it does not register an agent's room-pattern subscription. Configure SIP room placement and explicit named agent dispatch separately.

chapters.title: Recording consent with AgentTask
chapters.assessment: Use the pinned typed, awaited AgentTask pattern rather than Agent(tasks=[...]). Recording consent is a separate product policy/evidence stream from exact quote confirmation, and asking a question does not start or stop Egress.

chapters.title: DTMF & keypad input
chapters.assessment: Add bounded keypad collection as an optional phone-input example: correlated caller, digit/terminator limits, timeout and cancellation. Protect PIN-like data from transcript/trace exposure; verify the actual task/configuration API before copying it.

chapters.title: HD voice & secure trunking
chapters.assessment: Correct codec/configuration assumptions using current SIP references. Do not equate room Opus support with SIP-trunk Opus negotiation or present TLS/SRTP as an end-to-end application privacy guarantee.

chapters.title: Making outbound calls
chapters.assessment: Introduce outbound dialing as a new external effect: caller readiness, create-call ambiguity, bounded ringing and safe reconciliation. A transport timeout cannot independently authorize another chargeable dial attempt.

chapters.title: Test from your phone
chapters.assessment: Retain actual-phone testing as evidence distinct from a browser demo, with separate signaling, audio and agent observations. Course latency targets are examples, not measured POC SLOs or universal thresholds.

courses.decision: Add the missing telephony mental model, especially the separation between SIP routing and named-agent dispatch.
courses.treatment: Introduce one telephony diagram and targeted questions. Keep carrier provisioning and legal sufficiency claims outside the local POC's implementation claims.
courses.review_summary: Recommend a short telephony foundation bridge: SIP versus RTP, caller/room/agent dispatch separation, keypad input and outbound-call uncertainty. Defer provider shopping and provisioning walkthroughs.

courses.title: Tools, Tasks & Workflows

chapters.title: Workflow architecture
chapters.assessment: The distinction between a conversational agent, a focused temporary task and a multistep conversational group fills a real SDK gap. Session control-flow completion is separate from P1’s persisted accepted-work authority and crash recovery. REC-P1-01 should explicitly distinguish AgentTask, beta conversational TaskGroup and asyncio.TaskGroup.

chapters.title: Building the greeter agent
chapters.assessment: A small persona with clear tools and a handoff is a useful framework example. The displayed self.hand_off call is not the pinned API, and returning a transfer announcement alone does not prove that the target agent took control. Use an actual return-based tool handoff or an explicit current-session update_agent contract, then assert the observed transition.

chapters.title: Complex tool definitions
chapters.assessment: Reusable schemas and toolsets are relevant to SDK design. The examples use a Tool.create factory, Toolset construction/decorators and ToolFlag names that differ from the installed SDK. An LLM-supplied item price also must not become authoritative. Add a short pinned function_tool/toolset example and validate prices and authorization at a trusted domain boundary.

chapters.title: AgentTask: structured data collection
chapters.assessment: Temporary multi-turn collection returning a typed value is useful. In 1.8.11 the task is awaited directly, output_type is not a constructor parameter, and the generic result type is not runtime validation. Cancellation returning None also needs a matching optional result contract. REC-P1-01 should require explicit result validation and explain what survives a process crash.

chapters.title: TaskGroup: multi-step flows
chapters.assessment: The conversation can revisit previously collected information, but that is not a rollback of an external booking. The shown top-level import, instance-based add, run, list result and regress(index) interface do not match the pinned beta implementation. Teach factories with stable task IDs and keyed results. Treat the advertised runtime task addition as unsupported by the copied example until its scheduling semantics are proved.

chapters.title: Prebuilt tasks
chapters.assessment: Reusing focused email/address/DTMF collection is a useful SDK composition pattern. Python prebuilt workflows live under beta.workflows in the installed package. Collecting payment or identity data still needs domain validation, data handling and authorization outside a conversational result. Mention a small verified prebuilt example, its beta compatibility boundary and the separate business validation step.

chapters.title: Agent handoffs & context
chapters.assessment: Explicit persona transition and selected context transfer are useful. on_exit is an ordinary lifecycle hook, not guaranteed crash recovery. AgentConfigUpdate is a history item in this SDK, not a session update payload for the threshold shown. Link the corrected handoff example to explicit model inheritance and resource cleanup, without treating a spoken transfer message as the transition receipt.

chapters.title: State with userdata
chapters.assessment: The lesson eventually acknowledges in-memory state, which is the right limit. Typed userdata improves programming ergonomics but is neither automatically trusted input nor persistence. Writing only on_exit can lose state on abrupt process death. REC-P1-02 should separate transient conversational state, trusted rehydrated observations and authoritative durable state.

chapters.title: Dynamic tool management
chapters.assessment: Changing exposed tools can reduce model confusion during a workflow phase. The chapter’s claim that decorated tools remain unaffected is incorrect for update_tools: the new list replaces the agent’s list. Availability also does not revoke already admitted external work. Use a replacement-list example and ask where the business authorization is checked when a model invokes a stale tool.

chapters.title: Testing the workflow
chapters.assessment: Testing handoffs, state and correction paths is useful, but the displayed AgentTest/get_response/say harness is not present in the pinned SDK. Conditional assertions that only check a handoff if it happened can silently miss the required behavior. Use REC-P1-08 with AgentSession.run event assertions and explicit negative paths; do not label provider-backed model tests offline.

courses.decision: Add conversational tools, tasks and handoffs as explicit framework abstractions, with source-correct construction and lifecycle semantics.
courses.treatment: Distinguish AgentTask and the SDK workflow TaskGroup from asyncio.TaskGroup and P1's durable authority.
courses.review_summary: Conversational control-flow primitives are underrepresented in the existing book. Teach the actual pinned AgentTask and beta TaskGroup APIs, explicit runtime validation and model inheritance, while retaining P1 as the durable authority.

courses.title: Turn Detection & Conversation Quality

chapters.title: Turn detection fundamentals
chapters.assessment: The signal-versus-policy distinction is useful. STT can stream while speech is in progress; it need not wait for VAD speech-end before beginning. The lesson’s TurnDetectionOptions examples are not the installed API. REC-P1-03 should walk one audio turn through concurrent recognition, endpointing and durable admission without inventing serial stage waits.

chapters.title: VAD configuration
chapters.assessment: Sensitivity, silence windows and speech padding are valuable operational controls. Several displayed parameter names differ from Silero’s documented names. VAD silence and endpointing delay are not always simply additive; the controlling mode and timing anchor matter. Use actual names/units from the selected plugin release and measure clipping, false speech and end-to-end response latency on representative audio.

chapters.title: Multilingual turn detection
chapters.assessment: Language-specific pauses are useful evaluation cases. The Academy describes the text MultilingualModel as an acoustic model detecting language and prosody; the official contract uses STT text and STT-reported language. Newer audio turn detectors are a separate versioned option. REC-P1-03 should name the selected detector and its required inputs, including a separate STT path if a realtime provider lacks timely transcripts.

chapters.title: Endpointing configuration
chapters.assessment: Minimum and maximum waits express a responsiveness-versus-cutoff tradeoff, but their meaning depends on VAD/STT/text detector or realtime mode. A maximum endpointing delay is not a universal wall-clock cancellation deadline for all recognition and model work. Include mode-specific timing anchors in REC-P1-03 and avoid language/age presets as unvalidated universal recommendations.

chapters.title: Adaptive interruption handling
chapters.assessment: The distinction between backchannel and intentional barge-in is worth learning. Adaptive handling is audio-model inference rather than a general conversational LLM classifier, and false_interruption_timeout controls recovery after interruption rather than delaying the original interruption. REC-P1-04 should contrast onset thresholds, output pause/interruption and later resume, then preserve separate business cancellation semantics.

chapters.title: Backchanneling & natural flow
chapters.assessment: Short acknowledgments may mean continue, while a short command such as stop may be a real interruption. Word count alone cannot classify intent, and the lesson repeats the incorrect LLM/timeout explanation from the prior chapter. Add contrasting labeled audio cases to REC-P1-04 rather than copying a fixed timeout recipe.

chapters.title: A/B testing & quality metrics
chapters.assessment: Controlled variants and explicit latency/quality metrics are useful additions to preparation. The sample calls fewer than three words a false interruption, which mislabels genuine short commands. A fixed hundred calls is not a statistically justified sample for every target effect. REC-P1-08 can add labeled turn events, stratification by noise/language, explicit measurement boundaries and confidence intervals.

courses.decision: Deepen turn-quality tuning with measurable false interruption and endpointing outcomes rather than a universal setting.
courses.treatment: Expand LK-04/LK-05 and FAIL-02; preserve the difference between observed recognition, durable intake and completed output.
courses.review_summary: Separate VAD, STT text, text versus newer audio turn detectors, adaptive interruption onset and false-interruption recovery. Evaluation must use labeled audio and well-defined boundaries, not a word-count proxy.

courses.title: Pipeline Nodes, Hooks & Custom Logic

chapters.title: The voice pipeline architecture
chapters.assessment: Extension points are a strong SDK-role gap. However, nodes and hooks have different contracts; not every hook yields a stream. Lazy async iteration supports streaming but does not automatically prove globally bounded buffers, cancellation propagation or resource closure. REC-P1-05 should distinguish hook mutation, node transformation and independently owned work, using real signatures.

chapters.title: stt_node: audio preprocessing
chapters.assessment: Transforming speech events is useful for observation and safe input processing. The actual node consumes AsyncIterable audio frames plus ModelSettings, not a SpeechStream parameter. A keyword match can suggest escalation but cannot directly authorize account cancellation or another mutation. Fold a pass-through node and bounded validation into REC-P1-05; preserve source-turn identity before awaits as D2-07 already teaches.

chapters.title: llm_node: structured output
chapters.assessment: Structured output and text/audio separation are useful, but the examples conflate a ChatChunk delta object with a string and rely on fragile JSON extraction. A JSON object is not a validated schema, and a generated thinking field is not verified private reasoning. REC-P1-06 should bound buffering, validate the intended output and keep speech, tool calls and private diagnostics separate.

chapters.title: tts_node: emotional speech
chapters.assessment: Pronunciation and output transformation demonstrate valuable customization. The pinned TTS node consumes a text stream plus settings and emits AudioFrames. A shared last_emotion attribute can become stale or race across overlapping work; allocating provider clients per call also requires ownership. REC-P1-05 can show the real contract; REC-P1-06 should bind output metadata to the response that produced it.

chapters.title: on_user_turn_completed: RAG injection
chapters.assessment: Pre-generation retrieval is useful, but the example has the wrong hook shape and calls a nonexistent default hook. Returning normally continues; StopResponse explicitly aborts automatic reply generation. Retrieved text must remain untrusted evidence, with bounded I/O and validated scope. REC-P1-05 should contrast this hook with P2’s accepted-input-first gate; RAG enrichment itself creates no mutation authority.

chapters.title: Content filtering
chapters.assessment: This lesson exposes a concrete streaming failure: non-boundary chunks are yielded before the buffered sentence is cleaned. Its moderation parse failure also returns safe=True despite the safety comment. Transcript/display filtering cannot retract audio already sent to a realtime model or played out. REC-P1-06 should test forbidden text split across chunks, malformed moderation output, tools, cancellation and no unapproved output before release.

chapters.title: Realtime model nodes
chapters.assessment: An output-audio hook is a useful distinction for realtime models. Its actual signature includes ModelSettings. Timing first output inside that hook measures a local boundary, not full model/network/user-perceived latency. Text-only realtime plus separate TTS takes another supported path. REC-P1-07 should select hooks by actual configured modality, not assume every realtime session bypasses every text/TTS extension.

chapters.title: Full assembly
chapters.assessment: Assembly and observability are useful exercises, but the sample combines incompatible hooks and nonrepresentative mock event shapes. The retrieval helper closes the SQL connection only after success and creates a provider client without explicit closure. Hook duration is not full conversational latency. Use this as a code-review exercise after the smaller corrected nodes; mocks must exercise the SDK contract rather than teach an invented interface.

courses.decision: One of the largest useful gaps: exact streaming node contracts, bounded retrieval hooks and admission before output is released.
courses.treatment: Add hook/stream ownership and pre-output gate scenarios. Rewrite examples before use; the course filtering pattern can release original chunks before filtering.
courses.review_summary: Use the actual hook/node contracts and treat streaming output release as a correctness boundary. The Academy’s filter can leak raw text before approval, and its tests patch invented interfaces; proposed material should teach how to catch those errors.

courses.title: Realtime Models vs Pipelines

chapters.title: Architecture comparison
chapters.assessment: A cascaded pipeline and a turn-based speech-to-speech model trade observability, control and component choices. Neither architecture has a universal latency/quality ordering. LiveKit still orchestrates realtime sessions and supports mixed paths; it is not simply absent around the realtime provider. REC-P1-07 should compare actual input/output modalities and controls rather than brand names or a fixed three-stage-versus-zero-stage diagram.

chapters.title: Pipeline implementation
chapters.assessment: The provider substitution exercise usefully separates STT, text LLM and TTS choices. Its startup scaffold is incompatible with the pin and its component latency estimates are illustrative, not measurements of this POC. Streaming stages can overlap rather than add serially. A later lab can freeze the SDK/provider choices and measure real boundaries; no provider was invoked for this review.

chapters.title: OpenAI Realtime
chapters.assessment: Provider-native tools, turn detection and transcripts are useful concrete configuration topics. Preview model IDs, voices, modality details, prices and latency claims cannot be treated as a current compatibility contract. The shared Python entrypoint also needs correction. Use current provider/plugin documentation for an optional setup and preserve the project’s explicit provider mode and exact confirmation boundary.

chapters.title: Gemini Live
chapters.assessment: Provider differences matter, but a permanent OpenAI-audio-only versus Gemini-multimodal distinction is false. Supported modalities, voices, tools and session limits are specific to the selected API/model/plugin release. The architecture lesson is more useful than the comparison ranking. Coordinate exact provider configuration with the provider-course reviewer; do not infer tested support from this static tutorial.

chapters.title: Custom TTS with realtime models
chapters.assessment: A supported realtime model can understand audio and emit text for a separate TTS. That is a real gap worth adding. It requires text-only output support and explicit provider configuration; it is not automatically available for every realtime or full-duplex model. REC-P1-07 should explain control, timing and extra lifecycle/cost responsibilities, including a separate STT observer when appropriate.

chapters.title: Hybrid approaches
chapters.assessment: The architecture idea is useful, but the example’s PipelineAgent never overrides the inherited realtime models. Its constructor-only fallback can miss failures that occur when opening a provider session later. Switching agent persona or constructing a client is not proof of a healthy fallback path. Use REC-P1-07 to require explicit model overrides, controlled transition policy and fresh measured output; preserve original business operation identity during any fallback.

chapters.title: Latency & quality comparison
chapters.assessment: Consistent boundaries, percentiles and varied prompts are useful evaluation design. The published benchmark tables have no linked corpus, raw runs or artifacts, and the skeleton leaves prompt execution unimplemented. They cannot establish measured rankings or a qualified benchmark for this application. Extend REC-P1-08 with captured speech-end/first-audible-output boundaries, sample size, failures, region/version provenance and independent quality labels.

chapters.title: Choosing your architecture
chapters.assessment: The decision should start from output control, quality, modality support, operability and cost constraints. The chapter’s fixed prices and broad model/domain rankings are snapshots or unsupported generalizations. The existing book already encourages evidence-bounded engineering choices. Use the corrected REC-P1-07 decision scenario instead of adding another generic architecture checklist.

courses.decision: Expand architectural selection between pipeline, native realtime and hybrid configurations using measured constraints.
courses.treatment: Add a pipeline comparison and a provider experiment. Avoid fixed latency and cost promises or assuming every pipeline hook exists in realtime mode.
courses.review_summary: Modality support, control and observability are more useful than static brand rankings. Correct model inheritance and lazy connection health, then evaluate actual audio under explicit provider and durability policy.
