proposals.title: A conversational task is not a durable workflow
proposals.question: When would you use AgentTask, the conversational TaskGroup, asyncio.TaskGroup, or P1 accepted work?
proposals.answer: Use AgentTask for a focused multi-turn exchange that temporarily controls the current session and returns a value. In pinned 1.8.11 await the task instance; complete(result) settles its future, but a generic result annotation does not validate the value. Validate collected data explicitly. The beta conversational TaskGroup sequences factories identified by stable IDs and returns keyed results; revisiting a step changes conversational collection, not an external receipt. asyncio.TaskGroup instead owns related Python tasks and their failures within a process. P1 provides the persisted acceptance, issuance, receipts and recovery contract when business work must outlive that process.

followups.question: If a user corrects an earlier address, what is rolled back?
followups.answer: The conversational group can collect the address again and replace its derived result. Any already committed external operation keeps its original identity and receipt; a new change needs the domain’s own revision and authorization contract.

followups.question: Does AgentTask[Address] ensure complete(value) contains an Address?
followups.answer: No. In this pin complete stores the supplied value or exception. Construct and validate a runtime model or validate at the consuming boundary; type hints guide tools and static analysis rather than proving domain validity.

proposals.rationale: Adds concrete framework mechanics; existing project authority and durability answers remain the source of application guarantees.

proposals.title: Keep context useful without promoting it to authority
proposals.question: How would you preserve a returning caller’s context while keeping userdata, chat history and durable state distinct?
proposals.answer: Construct userdata explicitly from trusted, scoped reads; room or token metadata does not automatically hydrate AgentSession. Keep it as a convenient session object, not the source of consent or recovery. ChatContext contains messages, function calls, outputs and transition/configuration items. Trimming a messages-only list can orphan tool relationships or lose important context. Use the selected SDK’s context operations and retain the domain facts needed for current reasoning. For this POC, P2 rehydration loads authorized observations with separate as-of boundaries; P1 remains the business authority. Summaries and retrieved text help the model answer but cannot approve a mutation.

followups.question: Why is persisting only on_exit insufficient?
followups.answer: A normal handoff may run the hook, but abrupt process loss may prevent it. Persist accepted business facts at their own authority boundary. Treat conversational state snapshots as recoverable convenience with an explicit replay/hydration policy.

followups.question: May old tool output be summarized into a system instruction?
followups.answer: A summary remains a derived observation. Preserve provenance, scope and any freshness limits, and frame retrieved content as data. A system-message role alone must not grant the summarized material authority over domain guards.

proposals.rationale: Adds concrete framework mechanics; existing project authority and durability answers remain the source of application guarantees.

proposals.title: Name the signal that ends the turn
proposals.question: Explain how VAD, streaming STT, text end-of-turn detection and realtime provider turn control differ.
proposals.answer: VAD estimates whether the audio contains speech. Streaming STT produces provisional/final text while audio is arriving. The text MultilingualModel uses STT conversation context and STT-reported language to estimate whether a turn is complete; it is not the adaptive audio-interruption classifier. Endpointing applies a mode-specific wait policy, so do not blindly add every configured silence delay. A realtime provider can own turn control instead, or a supported integration can supply separate STT and choose the framework detector. Select one controlling path. The POC’s manual P2 path additionally requires durable intake before its dispatched generation; recognizing a final transcript alone does not satisfy that invariant.

followups.question: What changed in newer official turn-detector guidance?
followups.answer: Current documentation also describes an audio detector and deprecates the text detector for a future major version. State the chosen plugin and release; do not attribute the audio model’s inputs or timing behavior to the text MultilingualModel.

followups.question: Does max endpointing delay cap all response latency?
followups.answer: No. It controls a turn-ending policy in its selected mode. Transcript availability, model calls, tools, synthesis, transport and playout have other timing boundaries and need their own budgets and observations.

proposals.rationale: Adds concrete framework mechanics; existing project authority and durability answers remain the source of application guarantees.

proposals.title: Separate interruption onset from recovery
proposals.question: An agent stops speaking on background noise and later resumes. Which controls would you inspect, and what must business work do?
proposals.answer: Inspect the actual turn/interruption mode, VAD quality, onset minimum duration/word thresholds and adaptive detector observations. false_interruption_timeout is not a delay before stopping speech: it governs silence after an interruption, when the framework can identify a false interruption and resume without user transcription. In this pin the activity can pause output before this recovery decision. A short stop can be a real command, while a longer acknowledgment can still be feedback, so use labeled representative audio. Preserve the accepted P1/P2 operation and output observations. Interruption stops or pauses conversation output; business cancellation requires its own explicit policy and cannot erase a possible external effect.

followups.question: Should increasing the recovery timeout prevent the initial cutoff?
followups.answer: No. It changes how long recovery waits after the interruption. To address onset false positives, inspect the selected audio signal and onset/adaptive controls, then measure cutoff and resume behavior separately.

followups.question: How would you evaluate the setting?
followups.answer: Label intended stops, backchannels, noise and silence across languages and environments. Measure false interruption, missed interruption, output stop/resume latency and user task outcomes; word count alone is not ground truth.

proposals.rationale: Adds concrete framework mechanics; existing project authority and durability answers remain the source of application guarantees.

proposals.title: Respect the extension point contract
proposals.question: You want RAG before generation and pronunciation fixes before synthesis. Which extension points would you use and what must their code preserve?
proposals.answer: Use on_user_turn_completed(self, turn_ctx, new_message) for bounded pre-generation enrichment. Its default body is pass; returning normally continues, while StopResponse explicitly stops automatic reply generation. Keep retrieved text scoped, bounded and untrusted. For pronunciation, transform the asynchronous text stream in tts_node and forward ModelSettings to the default node, yielding AudioFrames. Other nodes have their own audio, context, tool and chunk contracts. Preserve cancellation and close any independently created resource; lazy iteration alone does not guarantee that. In the P2 manual adapter, this hook must also preserve the existing durable-admission order rather than create a competing intake path.

followups.question: Can you skip a default hook call to suppress the reply?
followups.answer: The default user-turn hook is a no-op in this pin. Use the documented StopResponse control path. That stops automatic reply generation, not a previously accepted business operation or an already possible supplier call.

followups.question: What should a node pass-through test assert?
followups.answer: Use real-shaped audio/events/chunks and the actual signature, including settings. Assert identity/order of preserved outputs, cancellation and owned-resource closure, then separately verify actual media if a user-audible claim is required.

proposals.rationale: Adds concrete framework mechanics; existing project authority and durability answers remain the source of application guarantees.

proposals.title: Approve streamed output before it escapes
proposals.question: How would you review a node that streams JSON response text to TTS while filtering disallowed content?
proposals.answer: Trace every yield and every buffer. If original chunks escape before a sentence is approved, a later replacement cannot retract spoken content. Bound retained bytes/time, handle malformed/incomplete structures explicitly, and validate the intended schema and domain values rather than merely parsing JSON. Respect the actual ChatChunk structure, including tool calls and other required metadata. Bind emotion or rendering metadata to the response that produced it rather than a mutable shared last value. Choose the latency cost of withholding output deliberately, test chunk-split forbidden patterns and failure paths, and keep sensitive generated reasoning out of logs. Display-only filtering is a separate boundary from audio release.

followups.question: Is fail-open always wrong on moderation failure?
followups.answer: The policy depends on the product, but it must be explicit and truthful. A parse failure is unknown, not a positive safe verdict. Decide whether to withhold, use a constrained fallback or escalate; test that branch independently.

followups.question: Can text filtering protect a realtime model from original audio?
followups.answer: Not if that audio has already been sent to the provider. Apply the required protection before that ingress boundary or select another architecture. Similarly, filtering a transcript after synthesis cannot retract published speech.

proposals.rationale: Adds concrete framework mechanics; existing project authority and durability answers remain the source of application guarantees.

proposals.title: Configure the hybrid you actually intend
proposals.question: How would you combine realtime audio understanding with controlled speech output, and prove a handoff really changed model paths?
proposals.answer: For a supported turn-based realtime model, configure text-only output and a separate TTS to control voice and scripted wording. Confirm the exact provider/plugin supports that modality; current full-duplex behavior is a distinct contract. A parallel STT observer can supply timely text when needed, but must not create competing turn authority. For a realtime-to-cascade handoff, configure the target agent’s STT, text LLM, TTS and turn policy explicitly. In this SDK unspecified models inherit from the session, so changing persona alone does not change the pipeline. Measure the resulting output path and own both providers’ lifetimes; do not infer health from successful client construction.

followups.question: Would separate TTS guarantee lower latency?
followups.answer: No. It adds another configured component and changes streaming, buffering, cost and output control. Compare the same workload and audible timing boundaries; provider load, utterance length and turn policy can dominate the result.

followups.question: How should fallback interact with durable work?
followups.answer: Use an explicit permitted model/provider transition and preserve the original accepted operation and receipts. Retrying conversation generation is not permission to repeat an uncertain business effect. Qualification must observe actual new-path output, not only a selected-mode badge.

proposals.rationale: Adds concrete framework mechanics; existing project authority and durability answers remain the source of application guarantees.

proposals.title: Test conversation quality without weakening correctness
proposals.question: What belongs in deterministic SDK tests, model-behavior evaluations and real audio experiments?
proposals.answer: Use deterministic tests for runtime schemas, tool/domain authorization, exact operation identities, output gating and resource ownership. Use AgentSession.run with explicit event assertions to check tool names, arguments, outputs and handoffs; model-generated wording or a semantic judge adds stochastic behavior and may call a provider. Keep credentials and costs in an explicit test lane. Real audio is still needed for recognition, turn-taking, noise, interruption and playout claims. Compare labeled representative cases with defined latency boundaries, failures, versions and sample sizes. A mock using invented event fields can pass while the installed integration fails, and an illustrative benchmark table is not evidence for this application.

followups.question: What if a semantic judge is flaky?
followups.answer: Inspect failed transcripts and the intended behavior first. Calibrate the rubric against human labels and repeat a declared evaluation set. Keep hard business invariants deterministic; do not broaden the rubric merely to turn unexplained failures green.

followups.question: Which latency number would you publish?
followups.answer: Name the start and finish precisely, such as observed user speech end to first rendered agent audio, and disclose measurement limitations. Report distribution, failures, sample count, region and version; keep model TTFB and hook duration as separate supporting metrics.

proposals.rationale: Adds concrete framework mechanics; existing project authority and durability answers remain the source of application guarantees.

proposals.title: A token endpoint is an authorization boundary
proposals.question: Your frontend asks for a room token and supplies roomName and participantName. Which values can the server trust, and what must it decide itself?
answer: A valid room JWT proves that a server signed particular claims. It does not prove that the person calling your token endpoint was entitled to those claims. I would authenticate the application user first, resolve their permitted account and conversation on the server, choose an allowed participant identity, and grant only the required room/media/data capabilities. A display name can remain user supplied, but it must not select another customer's case or grant administrative powers. Signing credentials stay server-side; keeping them there is one control, not the whole authorization design.

I would also authorize agent selection and validate bounded dispatch metadata. The room grant lets a participant connect; it does not grant a model or browser permission to confirm a booking. For an interview failure case, I would submit a valid logged-in user's request naming another account's room, then check that issuance fails before dispatch. This is a proposed frontend exercise. The POC's trusted P2 construction and separate exact confirmation are related examples, not evidence that its console implements the Academy React template.

followups.question: Does a short token lifetime remove the need to authenticate this endpoint?
followups.answer: No. An attacker can obtain another fresh token while issuance remains open. Token lifetime limits one credential's validity; the issuer still needs application authentication, authorization, bounded admission and a documented revocation/recovery policy.

followups.question: Can a participant attribute safely contain a role?
followups.answer: It can carry a backend-issued claim if the design prevents the participant from rewriting it and verifies its trusted origin. A mutable self-asserted attribute cannot grant business authority. Prefer a server-side principal binding for consequential operations.

proposals.rationale: Concrete frontend credential-minting threat model is absent from the current book's lower-level trusted construction discussion.

proposals.title: Choose RPC, synchronized state or a durable command
proposals.question: A browser can call an availability RPC and display a confirmation topic. How would you prevent those convenient realtime APIs from becoming an unsafe booking protocol?
answer: I would use a bounded RPC for a request whose response is useful immediately, such as a permitted availability read. The handler still checks caller identity, application scope, schema, size and deadline; a room connection is not a general authorization grant. Low-frequency participant attributes can expose a compact current UI state, while text streams can carry incremental text. These mechanisms make the interface responsive, but none replaces a retained business command and its receipt.

A booking click should submit an exact proposal through the same authenticated case authority used by other channels, with a stable command identity and expected revision. After a response timeout, the UI reconciles that original command instead of displaying failure or generating a second booking. A missed confirmation card is recovered by an authorized backend read. I would test a successful commit followed by a dropped RPC response, then reconnect and verify one original result. In the POC, exact quote confirmation and retained P2 evidence demonstrate this boundary; the proposed RPC layer would be a separate adapter.

followups.question: Where is an RPC method registered in the pinned Python room SDK?
followups.answer: Register with room.local_participant.register_rpc_method(method_name, handler), or its decorator form. The handler receives RpcInvocationData, including caller_identity, and returns str. Call through room.local_participant.perform_rpc(...); response_timeout is in seconds in this Python API. RPC is separate from AgentSession events; a timeout does not prove the handler or an external effect stopped.

followups.question: Would synchronized attributes make the booking confirmation durable?
followups.answer: They help late joiners see current participant state within that room. They do not provide the business transaction, immutable command receipt or recovery identity. Render them as projections and reconcile important outcomes through the case authority.

proposals.rationale: Adds LiveKit-specific frontend mechanism selection and an ambiguous RPC response example without duplicating inbox theory.

proposals.title: A phone call needs two distinct dispatch decisions
proposals.question: A SIP caller appears in the expected room, but the named agent never joins. What does that observation establish, and what would you inspect next?
answer: The call has crossed at least the trunk and SIP-room placement boundaries. That does not establish named agent dispatch. The SIP dispatch rule chooses the caller's room, while room agent configuration chooses which registered agent job should enter it. A room prefix is a naming policy, not a subscription pattern that automatically registers an agent. I would inspect the matched trunk/rule, room configuration, registered agent_name, job acceptance and application readiness as separate observations.

I would then confirm which participant is the SIP caller and correlate its call identifiers with carrier and room logs. If the agent joins but the caller hears silence, I would move to media direction, negotiated codec, subscriptions and inference readiness instead of recreating dispatch rules. For a bounded test matrix, vary only one layer: wrong agent name, no dispatch entry, worker unavailable, then media blocked after successful join. This is interview preparation for a telephony extension; the POC's native rooms and simulated SMS do not establish a working PSTN integration.

followups.question: Can token-based dispatch repair an already existing room?
followups.answer: The current documented token room configuration is applied when the room is created. For a room that already exists, use an explicitly authorized dispatch API path rather than assuming a reconnecting participant's token replays room creation settings.

followups.question: What changes when collecting keypad digits?
followups.answer: Bind collection to the intended caller and supported DTMF events, cap digits and waiting time, and define cancellation/terminator behavior. Do not log PIN-like values or infer customer authentication merely because a SIP participant supplied digits.

proposals.rationale: The current book does not explain SIP room placement versus named agent dispatch.

proposals.title: A dial timeout is not permission to call twice
proposals.question: Your outbound-call request times out just as the customer's phone starts ringing. How would you design retry, capacity and user-visible status?
answer: I would retain the original authorized dial intent, immutable destination, local operation identity and any provider call correlation before treating a timeout as retryable. The timeout establishes that this waiter stopped receiving a result; it does not establish that no billable call leg exists. I would use only the provider's documented reconciliation and idempotency contract. If the supported evidence cannot resolve the possible call, the application retains unknown rather than silently dialing again through another trunk.

Admission should bound both call-start rate and live call concurrency, with separate budgets for control and observation. A timed-out waiter must not free a slot while a known physical call is still active. Calling policy, suppression, destination and current permission must be checked for a genuinely new attempt. I would test response loss after dialing, delayed answer, a process restart and a later cancellation request. These are proposed phone scenarios: they transfer lessons from P2 provider operations, not a claim that the POC's fake-SMS retry contract applies to SIP carriers.

followups.question: Is exponential backoff enough to make the retry safe?
followups.answer: It reduces retry pressure but does not establish nonacceptance. First decide whether another external call is permitted under the original operation's contract; only then choose bounded timing, jitter, current permission and carrier-capacity policy.

followups.question: What should be counted as success?
followups.answer: Track request admission, provider call creation, ringing, answer and application completion separately. A voicemail or IVR can answer a call. A transport-level result must not be presented as a verified human conversation or completed business task.

proposals.rationale: Phone-specific adaptation of existing uncertainty and backpressure concepts; useful as a scenario box rather than a duplicate foundational chapter.

proposals.title: Transfer a live call without inventing a human receipt
proposals.question: How would you choose between a cold transfer, a warm transfer and a specialist agent handoff, and recover when the human never answers?
answer: A cold phone transfer forwards the existing SIP caller through the provider, commonly using REFER; it can end the caller's LiveKit session. A warm transfer keeps ownership while the caller waits, creates a private consultation with the intended human, supplies bounded context, then connects the parties after the workflow permits it. A session-local conversational agent handoff changes active behavior, while P3 specialist delegation produces a separately validated asynchronous result. These are distinct control and evidence boundaries.

For a warm workflow I would track caller hold, destination dial, human answer, consultation, merge and cleanup explicitly. The private briefing must not leak to the caller or another room. On no answer, return to the caller with a truthful fallback rather than abandoning them on hold. I would bind the original caller identity and separately authorize the transfer destination. A generated summary is an aid to the human, not authority to approve a refund. This is a proposed telephony exercise, not a feature implied by the POC's durable result receiver.

followups.question: Does successful REFER prove that a human has taken responsibility?
followups.answer: No. Provider-reported forwarding success can include voicemail or an IVR, and LiveKit no longer observes the forwarded call afterward. Record the exact supported transfer outcome; obtain a separate application acknowledgement if human ownership matters.

followups.question: What if the caller hangs up during the private briefing?
followups.answer: Cancel or close owned consultation/dial work through the supported workflow, observe actual resource termination and avoid merging an orphaned human leg. Keep the original transfer observations; a local cancelled waiter does not prove that the external leg stopped.

proposals.rationale: Live call consultation/privacy/merge semantics are absent from the current asynchronous delegation coverage.

proposals.title: Recording permission and a recording artifact are different facts
proposals.question: An agent asked for recording consent, but the recording API timed out. What state should the application retain and what must it avoid claiming?
answer: I would separate the product's consent policy and evidence from the recording operation itself. A typed conversational task can collect a result, but the application must validate and retain whatever evidence its policy requires. That outcome is not a booking confirmation, a general customer authorization or proof that recording started. The recorder is a separate media consumer; starting it, observing active capture and verifying a finalized output object are separate facts.

I would retain a stable recording intent and correlate supported Egress identifiers and status observations before choosing a recovery action. An unknown start must not become a second recorder or a false promise that nothing was captured. Access, retention and redaction are deliberate product requirements, with legal policy supplied by the organization rather than inferred from a tutorial. I would test refusal, delayed consent, start-response loss, partial output and finalization failure. This is a design exercise; the POC's playback evidence and demo video do not establish an implemented compliant call-recording service.

followups.question: Should a recording task be configured as Agent(tasks=[...])?
followups.answer: That constructor is not supported by the inspected Agents 1.8.11 source. Use the release's typed task/await workflow in an active agent context, and keep its conversational result separate from application-owned recording admission and lifecycle.

followups.question: Does a separate Egress process eliminate performance and privacy concerns?
followups.answer: It separates ownership but still requires resource budgeting, correct subscriptions and output handling. Recordings also introduce another plaintext consumer and retained artifact. Neither process separation nor encryption labels establish that every desired policy is satisfied.

proposals.rationale: Adds recording operation/output lifecycle, distinct from existing speech generation/playback observations.

proposals.title: Carry context to a human without promoting it to authority
proposals.question: A CRM match and an LLM-generated handoff summary say the caller is verified and a refund is approved. What would you trust, transmit and recheck?
answer: I would distinguish enrichment, verification and action authority. A phone-number match can suggest a CRM record; it does not independently authenticate the person speaking. Retrieved CRM notes, transcripts and generated summaries are data that may be stale, mistaken or adversarial. Verification status and approved actions should be read from trusted application records, with source identifiers and timestamps, instead of accepted because a summary states them confidently.

For the handoff I would send only the context the intended recipient needs, authenticated and bound to the original caller/case. The human's desktop projection and the live phone transfer are separate deliveries; one can succeed while the other fails. A summary should mark unresolved questions and possible external effects explicitly. I would deadline-bound enrichment so a slow CRM does not block a greeting, and give durable writeback its own command identity and recovery contract. This extends the book's source/authority distinction to a contact-center scenario; it is not a claim that the POC integrates Salesforce or HubSpot.

followups.question: Which LiveKit value contains a SIP caller's phone number?
followups.answer: The documented SIP participant attributes include sip.phoneNumber when available; it can be hidden. Room metadata is application-defined, so a phone number belongs there only under an explicit trusted contract. Select the intended participant rather than the first arbitrary room member.

followups.question: Should the full transcript become the next agent's system instructions?
followups.answer: No. Pass a bounded, explicitly scoped history or summary as data, while retaining the next agent's trusted policy. Preserve original records separately and label generated conclusions. Do not let a context transfer widen tools or grant mutation authority.

proposals.rationale: Contact-center trust and coordinated human delivery add a useful concrete scenario, though this can remain a sidebar if space is constrained.

proposals.title: Bound visual context and prove which scene was analyzed
proposals.question: How would you add screen understanding and document uploads while preventing stale visual answers, unbounded work and false delivery guarantees?
answer: I would make each visual observation identifiable: authorized source participant, track or upload reference, capture time, frame/document digest and viewport or scene revision where needed. A bounded sampler retains only the permitted recent context; it does not make old imagery current. If the answer depends on a screen that has changed, the agent should request or analyze a fresh observation. Images and extracted text remain untrusted data, and a model's confidence or schema-valid output does not establish factual accuracy.

A PDF should use a bounded byte stream or authenticated object reference, not one arbitrarily large reliable data packet. Validate actual bytes and declared size, bound parsing/decompression away from the audio loop, and record completion only after the selected receipt checks succeed. Screen annotations should refer to their source frame and expire rather than point at a moved button. I would test partial upload, reconnect, switched screen source, oversized input and stale annotation. The POC already has a bounded scripted PNG fixture; continuous video and general document execution remain proposed extensions.

followups.question: Would E2EE keep the vision agent from seeing the user's content?
followups.answer: An agent that analyzes encrypted media must be an authorized decrypting endpoint with matching keys. E2EE can protect content from intermediaries; it does not hide plaintext from the agent or downstream model providers that process it. Draw that trust boundary explicitly.

followups.question: How would you choose frame rate and resolution?
followups.answer: Start from the task's detail and freshness requirements, set resource/token ceilings and measure latency, bytes and actual model usage. Avoid fixed per-frame token tables. Dropping stale frames can be safer than processing every queued image after the scene changed.

proposals.rationale: Adds time-varying visual provenance and large-file transport beyond the existing single immutable PNG evidence path.

proposals.title: Evaluate quality without voting away correctness
proposals.question: A prompt change improves average judge scores but occasionally repeats a booking. How would you evaluate and release it?
answer: Keep the no-duplicate-effect assertion as a deterministic release requirement against authoritative receipts and an independent supplier observation. A higher tone or relevance score cannot compensate for an unauthorized or repeated action. Run language-quality evaluation alongside those invariants, with separate outcomes rather than one blended score.

Freeze representative scenarios, source data, prompt/model/tool versions, judge rubric and judge version. Include ambiguity, refusal, wrong-tool arguments, interruption and no-source cases. Compare baseline and candidate on the same scenarios with repeated runs where justified; inspect uncertainty, severity and subgroup failures. Calibrate a held-out sample against human labels and retain disagreements. The proposed evaluation adds evidence about language behavior; it does not establish returned audio, physical cleanup or production capacity. Current book ROLE-07 states the boundary but does not teach this evaluation design.

followups.question: Can the LLM judge decide whether a supplier mutation happened?
followups.answer: No. Judge language against a rubric; read the business authority and independent supplier records for execution truth. A fluent confirmation sentence may be false, while an ACK loss may hide a committed action.

followups.question: When may a baseline change?
followups.answer: After an intentional reviewed change, with a retained old manifest and an explanation of expected differences. Do not replace it simply to turn a failing run green. Unobserved or skipped required checks remain nonpassing.

proposals.rationale: An operational plan for calibrated model-quality evaluation and regression evidence.

proposals.title: Canary new sessions while old work remains owned
proposals.question: How would you compare a new agent version without disrupting an ongoing call or repeating background work?
answer: Assign each new conversation to a recorded version/cohort at a trusted dispatch boundary, then keep that assignment stable for its defined lifetime. Record prompt, model, tools and application versions. Run the old and new populations with comparable workload and observe errors, usable first audio and useful task outcomes; explicitly account for timeouts and unresolved business work.

Stop new admission to an old owner before draining its sessions and actual I/O. Session shutdown, an SFU room drain and P1 business-worker recovery have distinct owners. A deployment change must not mint a fresh business identity for an ambiguous earlier command. Define a finite drain deadline and recovery behavior before rollout, plus rollback criteria based on measured harm. Current Cloud documentation describes a bounded old-session completion window; it is not permission to promise arbitrary calls finish forever. The POC has no measured Cloud canary, so this remains a design exercise extending SCALE-06.

followups.question: What does rollback actually undo?
followups.answer: It changes the selected version for eligible future work under the deployment contract. It does not retract spoken audio, reverse supplier effects or erase an accepted command. Reconcile original identities when earlier outcomes are uncertain.

followups.question: Why avoid assigning each turn randomly?
followups.answer: It confounds evaluation with changing prompts, tools or memory within one conversation and can violate compatibility. Choose and record the experimental unit; if turn-level experiments are intentional, define their state and permission semantics explicitly.

proposals.rationale: Version/cohort identity, experiment comparability and finite rollout recovery.

proposals.title: Observe the conversation and count the committed outcome
proposals.question: Why can a session have low model latency and high booking counts while users receive no useful result?
answer: Those counters may measure the wrong facts. LLM generation duration excludes parts of the user-perceived path; an agent-local booked flag or tool attempt does not prove a committed supplier change or a delivered completion. Correlate a chosen user input with turn/media observations and the original durable business operation, then count outcomes from retained authoritative receipts.

Keep component, turn, session and business measures separately named. In the pinned Python SDK, metrics_collected contains one typed metric and is deprecated for usage tracking; inspect session usage updates, per-message latency and session-report lifecycle for the selected version. Collect numeric usage in its actual units, preserving missing/unknown values. Use finite aggregate labels and access-controlled sampled traces for identity joins. A replay can add a new observation without adding a new booking. The new exercise would test that distinction rather than repeat the book's general instruction to add observability.

followups.question: Can you estimate cost from a session's wall duration?
followups.answer: Not reliably. Reconcile the actual provider billing quantities: audio seconds or tokens, text tokens, generated characters and other charges under a dated tariff. Include retries and unsuccessful attempts; label estimates and reconcile them with billing.

followups.question: Does a completed report prove the user heard the reply?
followups.answer: No. Pipeline and session observations describe their boundaries. Received/decoded/browser playout evidence is separate, and even playout does not establish human understanding or consent. Preserve that uncertainty in the dashboard and incident narrative.

proposals.rationale: A concrete telemetry-contract and duplicate-counting exercise.

proposals.title: Bound retrieval at the original turn
proposals.question: Where would you retrieve private knowledge for a voice reply, and what if the lookup returns after interruption?
answer: Choose between initial context, an explicit retrieval tool and a turn-completion hook based on whether information is stable, optional or needed before generation. The pinned Python hook receives turn_ctx and new_message; query the accepted message rather than a mutable global transcript. Use bounded asynchronous database/API clients or correctly owned offload, limit retrieved bytes/chunks and carry the original trusted scope and turn identity.

A local timeout or barge-in changes the waiting conversation, not necessarily the lifetime of a running database operation. Retain actual ownership until settlement, and recheck the original generation/lifecycle binding before incorporating the result. Never inject late data into whichever turn happens to be current. Use a truthful no-source or pending response and measure the selected latency boundary; 400 ms is an example budget, not a platform guarantee. Retrieval content remains untrusted evidence and cannot authorize P1 action. The repository's existing fixed-policy records are not a general RAG implementation.

followups.question: Should retrieval run for every utterance?
followups.answer: Only under a deliberate product design. Greetings may need no lookup; structured account facts may belong behind an authenticated tool. Unnecessary retrieval adds cost, exposure and delay. Compare approaches with a representative task and a measured budget.

followups.question: May a retrieved policy instruct the agent to approve a change?
followups.answer: No. Source text cannot grant permissions or replace exact human confirmation. Keep trusted instructions and application authority separate, enforce scope at source access, and test adversarial documents as inert evidence.

proposals.rationale: Version-correct retrieval timing and stale asynchronous result handling.

proposals.title: Cache evidence without leaking scope or inventing support
proposals.question: Two users ask the same policy question. When may you reuse the cached retrieval and cite it?
answer: Equivalent wording is only one input. Authorize the second user independently and bind reuse to the permitted tenant/account/document set, document/index version, retrieval configuration and other context that affects the answer. Store original chunk/source/version identifiers and invalidate or revalidate when access or evidence changes. Bound entries and bytes; a TTL is not a complete memory or access policy.

Distinguish an exact normalized-key cache from semantic similarity search. The inspected course's SemanticCache performs the former despite storing an unused embedding/threshold. A real semantic cache needs measured false-hit behavior, especially for negation, numbers and nearly identical policies. On output, carry protected source metadata and speak a concise attribution suited to audio, while retaining inspectable citations in an authorized text view if available. A model naming a document does not prove support. Test unanswerable and conflicting-source queries and keep action permission at the existing exact guard.

followups.question: Does a matching document title establish factual support?
followups.answer: No. Check that the retained version and relevant passage support the claim. The P3 fixed-policy verifier can recompute a small synthetic rule; arbitrary policy prose requires its own retrieval and faithfulness evaluation and an abstention path.

followups.question: Why not clear only the visible answer card?
followups.answer: Presentation state is not the protected identity ledger or source-access contract. Cached retrieval, retained receipts and unresolved processing have different lifetimes. Define their invalidation separately instead of treating a hidden card as deleted authority.

proposals.rationale: Access-aware RAG caching and spoken citation verification.

proposals.title: Compose graph or MCP logic with one business authority
proposals.question: If you add LangGraph checkpoints or MCP tools, can they replace P1's durable work and exact confirmation?
answer: Not merely by being present. A graph checkpoint preserves the state defined by its checkpointer; MCP standardizes tool exposure and invocation. Neither automatically implements this project's original accepted bytes, exact confirmation, issued execution permission, effect uncertainty and receipt reconciliation. Decide which component owns each fact and keep one recovering owner for the accepted business obligation.

For an experiment, make graph/MCP nodes call narrow public adapters with stable original command identities. Scope graph thread lookup to authenticated conversation bindings and own the checkpointer/client lifecycle. Replaying a node after a crash must reconcile the original operation before any permitted re-invocation. Waiter timeout does not prove a remote effect stopped. Use the selected supported API: current official LiveKit LangChain documentation describes a Python LLMAdapter over a compiled graph; the pinned core exposes MCP server objects through mcp_servers. Do not infer TypeScript plugin parity, transparent function-calling compatibility or general workflow durability from an illustrative wrapper.

followups.question: Can a graph be the sole durable workflow authority instead?
followups.answer: Yes, as a separate explicit architecture with a defined fault model and demonstrated acceptance, consent, idempotency and effect protocol. That is a redesign to evaluate, not permission to let two independent recovery mechanisms own the same operation.

followups.question: Does a discovered typed MCP tool carry mutation consent?
followups.answer: No. Discovery and schema validation describe a callable interface. Bind authenticated scope and exact approved intent at the server-owned boundary, and preserve the external operation's reconciliation identity after uncertain acknowledgment.

proposals.rationale: Framework persistence and tool-protocol semantics compared with the concrete P1/P3 authority boundary.

proposals.title: Choose providers from a reproducible voice experiment
proposals.question: How would you choose an STT/LLM/TTS stack without trusting a provider ranking table?
answer: Define the actual task, languages/accents, noise, interruption patterns, tool schemas, privacy constraints and acceptable failure behavior. Freeze audio/scenario inputs and model/plugin/prompt versions. Keep other components fixed while changing one, then compare transcription errors, task/tool correctness, first rendered audio, interrupted output and useful completion under the same load and region. Report distributions and failures, not one attractive latency.

Price actual billable units for the selected product and date: STT may charge audio time or tokens, LLMs distinguish input/output/cache/audio units, and TTS may use characters or tokens. Include transport, telephony, hosting, retries and unsuccessful work as relevant. Compare cost per useful resolution alongside quality and privacy. Do not infer that realtime always wins latency, loses tools or costs a fixed multiple. The course tables offer hypotheses; current official capability/pricing and observed evidence must decide. In this checkout, scripted, local_real and provider_real qualifications remain distinct and no silent fallback is authorized.

followups.question: How do you calculate word error rate?
followups.answer: For a specified transcript corpus, WER = (substitutions + deletions + insertions) / reference-word count. Declare normalization and stratify important entities and conditions; one aggregate WER can hide failures on names, numbers or a minority language.

followups.question: Why not sum three average stage timings?
followups.answer: Streaming and endpointing create dependencies and overlap. Define the end-to-end start and finish directly, correlate supporting spans and compare compatible populations. A first provider byte or token is not necessarily first audible output to the caller.

proposals.rationale: A concrete quality/capability/cost selection method instead of unstable rankings.

proposals.title: Restore the right state after a self-hosted failure
proposals.question: If Redis and configuration backups are healthy, what can still be lost when a LiveKit node dies?
answer: Backups and coordination state do not reproduce a running node's WebRTC transports, live media buffers, agent process resources or the application's business receipts. Public self-hosted LiveKit uses Redis for shared room/routing coordination, with a room hosted on a node. Agent servers register over an outbound WebSocket; they are a separate deployment and failure boundary.

Draw an inventory of durable configuration/secrets under protected backup, cluster coordination, live media/session state, agent-local memory and P1 business state. Give each an RPO/RTO and recovery owner. A proposed restore drill should recover configuration with compatible binaries, establish a new usable connection and reconcile accepted business work against original receipts and supplier identities. Graceful room draining is different from forced node loss; forced termination may interrupt calls and leave business recovery pending. Verify configured metrics and network paths instead of assuming default /metrics on 7880. The current local POC has not demonstrated a redundant SFU or regional failover.

followups.question: Does a long Kubernetes termination grace period guarantee no dropped call?
followups.answer: No. It supplies a maximum opportunity to drain under the orchestrator's contract. Active calls may outlast it, dependencies may fail or a node may die abruptly. Define what is admitted, what is retained and how forced-loss recovery is observed.

followups.question: What does a successful health endpoint prove?
followups.answer: Only the endpoint's checks. Demonstrate authenticated connection, actual media in the selected paths and independently verified business progress for those claims. Keep media-server health, worker registration, provider readiness and durable-work recovery separately observable.

proposals.rationale: A state-by-state restore exercise spanning media, agents and business authority.

data.claim_location: Opening thesis; latency budget table; transport comparison
data.correction: WebRTC is a strong fit, not the sole possible voice transport. UDP media avoids TCP stream head-of-line delay but WebRTC can use TCP/TLS relays. Fixed transport/model latency ranges and a universal conversational threshold are not guarantees.
data.status: conceptual correction; numeric claims not independently qualified

data.claim_location: SFU scaling section and multi-region Redis/media-relay explanation
data.correction: Do not generalize the described cross-SFU room mesh to self-hosted LiveKit. Official self-hosted distributed documentation says one room fits on one node; Redis coordinates routing/signaling. Mesh/MCU/SFU participant cutoffs are workload-dependent, not architectural hard limits.

data.claim_location: Room metadata; participant kind; cheap rooms; related agent/service claims
data.correction: Room metadata is an opaque string; attributes are key/value pairs. Participant kind does not bypass grants. Common media primitives coexist with separate AgentServer, SIP, ingress and egress lifecycles. Room creation and forwarding still have resource limits.

data.claim_location: Reliability/ordering; transactional RPC; room metadata
data.correction: Reliable live delivery is not durable storage, replay or an atomic business transaction. Preserve operation identities and explicit acceptance when an RPC response is lost. Stream ordering has a defined stream/transport scope; metadata is not a database.

data.claim_location: E2EE key negotiation/rotation and encrypted application scope
data.correction: Application code must securely generate and distribute keys. An authorized agent can decrypt content it processes; a plaintext-consuming provider remains part of the trust path. Distinguish transport encryption from configured E2EE and from signaling/API visibility.

data.claim_location: Server and agent SDK parity tables; competitive breadth claims
data.correction: Shared abstractions do not promise identical plugins, APIs or features across languages and releases. Check the selected SDK/plugin release and platform; a catalogue or marketing breadth claim is not compatibility evidence.

data.claim_location: Feature tables; Flows description; interruption/state/deployment and adoption claims
data.correction: Treat competitor limitations, market adoption and quality rankings as unverified comparisons. Compare current primary APIs and a common workload. The useful architecture distinction does not justify a claim that competing frameworks lack state, interruption handling or deployment support.
data.status: comparative claims not independently established; do not repeat as facts

data.claim_location: Pricing, added latency, compliance and suitability tables; choosing-your-approach thresholds
data.correction: Prices, contract availability, regions, compliance configurations and model behavior change. This review makes no purchasing or regulatory recommendation from those tables. Volume alone cannot determine total cost; include engineering, operations, provider and migration costs.

data.claim_location: Python entrypoint and repeated scaffold in later lessons
data.correction: Pinned rtc_session supplies JobContext. Construct AgentSession (or configure Agent) with the selected models, then start it with the agent and room. Do not pass stt/llm/tts to start or treat the callback as a preconstructed AgentSession.

data.claim_location: MultimodalModel import; simplified events; automatic cleanup language
data.correction: Verify exported symbols and event payload objects against the pin. Realtime model plugins differ from a generic MultimodalModel import. Framework orchestration does not close every independently created task, client, database connection or application resource.

data.claim_location: Tool schemas; booking receipt; speech with interruptions disabled
data.correction: RunContext is injected where the supported signature declares it; it is not a universal mandatory first positional argument. In-memory appointment state and an utterance do not prove durable commitment, exact human consent, actual hearing or safe retry after unknown I/O.

data.claim_location: chat_ctx.messages trimming and automatic userdata hydration claims
data.correction: Use the actual heterogeneous ChatContext.items contract and preserve valid tool-call/output relationships. Session userdata must be explicitly constructed or assigned after trusted hydration; attaching data to a room/token does not automatically populate it. on_exit alone cannot make transient state crash-safe.

data.claim_location: No-network claim; model judges; displayed test construction
data.correction: Provider-backed generation or judging can make network calls. AgentSession.run/RunResult checks must match the installed API. Keep deterministic contract assertions, stochastic behavior evaluations and actual audio/browser gates separate. Do not weaken a judge merely to make an unexplained failure disappear.

data.claim_location: Noise and background-audio timing; cache; deployment/production-readiness assertions
data.correction: Avoid unqualified fixed latency, automatic cross-call caching or complete production-readiness claims. Plugin availability, audio processing, ownership and current lifecycle APIs need explicit qualification. Deployment/configuration health is not proof of inference, media, consent or business durability.

data.claim_location: self.hand_off; session.update_config(AgentConfigUpdate(...)); guaranteed on_exit
data.correction: Use the supported tool-return handoff or session.update_agent interface. AgentConfigUpdate records changes in conversation history, not the shown threshold configuration. on_exit may run on a normal transition but cannot guarantee writes survive abrupt process death.

data.claim_location: Tool.create; empty Toolset(); .tool decorator; ToolFlag examples
data.correction: The pinned Tool is abstract, Toolset requires an ID, and the shown flag names are absent. Use verified function_tool/toolset APIs. Model-provided prices and schema-valid values still require trusted domain validation and action authorization.

data.claim_location: output_type constructor; task.run(session); automatic typed completion
data.correction: AgentTask is directly awaitable and has no output_type argument here. Generic annotations do not validate complete(result); explicitly validate the returned structure/domain facts. A conversational task is not a durable queue, and None cancellation must fit the declared result contract.

data.claim_location: Top-level import; group.add(instance); group.run; list results; regress(index)
data.correction: Pinned TaskGroup is beta, accepts factories plus ID/description and returns keyed results when awaited. Its internal regression requeues conversational tasks; it cannot undo external effects. on_enter snapshots registered IDs, so arbitrary later additions are not established by this sample.

data.claim_location: Python prebuilt import and payment/identity examples
data.correction: The installed prebuilt tasks are under livekit.agents.beta.workflows, not the shown prebuilt.tasks package. Collection and type hints do not authenticate identity, authorize payment or establish business confirmation. Validate the selected task’s exact release contract. The SIP-only DTMF restriction is also too strong: room SDKs can publish DTMF messages and the task listens to room events.

data.claim_location: Claim that decorated tools remain unaffected; session update calls
data.correction: update_tools replaces the active agent’s tool list, including decorated tools unless explicitly retained. Use update_instructions/update_tools on the actual Agent API. Visibility is a model affordance; durable business guards must reject unauthorized stale calls independently.

data.claim_location: AgentTest import/get_response/say; conditional handoff assertion
data.correction: The displayed test harness is not the pinned framework’s public test API. Use AgentSession.run with explicit function/handoff/output assertions. An assertion inside an if-handoff branch does not prove a required handoff occurred. Model-backed tests remain a separate provider-capable lane.

data.claim_location: TurnDetectionOptions examples; serial STT story; VAD and endpoint arithmetic
data.correction: The pin exports TurnHandlingOptions with nested endpointing/interruption options, not the shown TurnDetectionOptions. Streaming STT can run during speech. Use Silero’s actual parameter names; VAD silence and endpoint waits depend on mode and timing anchors rather than a universal sum.

data.claim_location: Acoustic/prosodic language-detection explanation and multilingual_model flag
data.correction: The named MultilingualModel is a text end-of-turn model using STT context and language. Current docs also describe a different audio detector; do not retrofit that mechanism onto the text plugin. Its realtime use needs timely STT and one chosen turn-control path.

data.claim_location: Adaptive classifier; false-interruption timeout; repeated backchannel explanation
data.correction: Adaptive interruption is audio-model inference, not an ordinary LLM call for each backchannel. Onset thresholds and false-interruption recovery differ: the timeout follows the interruption/pause and can resume speech when no real transcript arrives. Business cancellation is another command.

data.claim_location: Short-word false-positive rule; sample-size prescription
data.correction: A short utterance can be an intentional stop command. Obtain ground-truth labels, stratify representative audio, define denominators and measurement boundaries, and choose sample size for the effect/confidence required. Completion rate alone can reward an agent for ignoring genuine interruptions.

data.claim_location: Signatures throughout node lessons and default user-turn hook
data.correction: Read actual node signatures: audio/text iterables, tools and ModelSettings must be forwarded. The user-turn hook receives history and the new message and normally returns None; it has no Agent.default counterpart. Async iteration alone does not prove boundedness or cleanup.

data.claim_location: ChatChunk.delta accumulation; JSON extraction; thinking logs; shared emotion
data.correction: A ChatChunk delta can carry structured content/tool metadata, not a raw string. Validate a bounded final structure before release, preserve required events and own the stream. A generated thinking field is not faithful private reasoning; avoid sensitive reasoning/transcript logging and shared response metadata races.

data.claim_location: OutputFilterAgent llm_node and IntentFilterAgent.check_intent Python blocks
data.correction: The filter yields raw non-boundary chunks before sentence approval, so later cleaning cannot retract leaked speech. Its JSON-error branch returns safe=True. Define an explicit unknown/failure policy, hold output until approved and bounded, and distinguish display filtering from audio/model ingress protection.

data.claim_location: Retrieval lifetime; MagicMock tests; hook-duration histogram
data.correction: Mocks model invented attributes and patch a nonexistent hook, so they cannot establish installed SDK compatibility. Own provider/SQL resources with exception-safe closure and bounded requests. The measured hook interval covers retrieval/enrichment, not speech-end-to-first-rendered-audio latency.

data.claim_location: Bypass claims; provider capability tables; custom TTS examples
data.correction: Realtime is a configured modality path, not a guarantee that all text/TTS hooks disappear. Supported turn-based models can emit text to separate TTS. Verify provider/model/plugin capabilities; current OpenAI image support contradicts an unconditional audio-only claim, and full-duplex has different constraints.

data.claim_location: PipelineAgent configuration and constructor-only fallback loop
data.correction: An agent without model overrides inherits the session’s models, so the illustrated persona handoff does not switch to a cascade. Creating a client may not connect it; lazy session failures bypass constructor-only fallback. Test explicit, authorized transitions and retain original business identities.

data.claim_location: 50-prompt benchmark assertion; MOS/cost/ranking tables; execution placeholder
data.correction: No linked corpus, raw observations or reproducible artifacts establish the published rankings. The harness leaves actual execution unimplemented. Define consistent audible boundaries, versions, region, failures, response lengths and quality labels; do not copy illustrative numbers as measured application results.

data.title: SIP room placement is not agent selection by room prefix
data.observed: The lessons repeatedly describe an agent registered for a room-name pattern and imply matching the SIP room prefix dispatches that agent.
data.correction: Treat the SIP rule as room placement. Configure agent dispatch separately, for example through room_config.agents with a registered agent_name. Validate the selected trunk/rule, room, dispatched job and actual agent readiness independently.
data.book_implication: Extend LK-02 with an explicit two-stage diagram; this is a gap in phone-specific explanation, not a correction to the book's current durable execution model.

data.title: Several code examples do not match the pinned Agents API
data.observed: Consent uses Agent(tasks=[...]); RPC uses an AgentSession rpc_request event; vision adds VideoFrameOptions/video_frame_options; UI state is presented as a universal six-state agent enum.
data.correction: The inspected Agent constructor has no tasks argument. AgentTask is awaited in active agent context. RPC registers on Room/LocalParticipant. The installed RoomInputOptions has video_enabled but no video_frame_options; use actual RoomOptions/video_input and AgentSession video_sampler surfaces as appropriate. Separate connection/UI state from the pinned AgentState literal.
data.book_implication: Treat Academy snippets as conceptual prompts until reconciled to the exact maintained package. Do not replace the book's tested SDK composition with these examples.

data.title: Keeping the signing secret server-side does not authorize the requester
data.observed: The token routes mint credentials without application-user authentication. The dispatch route accepts the requested room and participant identity from query parameters.
data.correction: Authenticate the application user, resolve room/business bindings server-side, explicitly restrict grants and prevent arbitrary dispatch choices. A user-supplied name is a display label until validated by an independent identity policy. Short token lifetime does not repair missing issuance authorization.
data.book_implication: Add a concrete frontend token-endpoint threat-model question alongside P2-11 and ROLE-05.

data.title: Reliable packets neither carry arbitrary files nor prove physical execution
data.observed: Document upload sends a whole file through one publishData packet. Both document and device-control prose treat reliable delivery as a guarantee of complete arrival.
data.correction: The documented reliable user-payload ceiling is 15 KiB, and reliable packets remain best effort with disconnection gaps. Use a bounded file/byte stream or authenticated object reference for documents. A hardware command also needs authorization, stable identity, expiry, an application receipt and independent device-state/safety handling.
data.book_implication: Extend RTC-06 with a file-transfer example; retain physical control only as an optional counterexample. Do not weaken existing P2 durable acceptance.

data.title: SIP codec configuration cannot be inferred from room Opus support
data.observed: The HD chapter prescribes allowed_codecs with Opus on SIPInboundTrunkInfo and promises a richer path without distinguishing trunk negotiation from room codecs.
data.correction: Current SIP references use media configuration, list G.722/PCMU/PCMA as defaults and document supported additions separately. The inspected protocol stub does not accept allowed_codecs. Read SDP and current trunk/provider support; an SDP example containing offered Opus is not proof that it is selected or supported by the deployed SIP bridge.
data.book_implication: Teach negotiation and measurement, with version-labelled configuration instead of copying this constructor.

data.title: Caller enrichment and generated summaries are not authentication or authority
data.observed: CRM integration takes the caller phone from room metadata and merges retrieved profile content into instructions. Escalation examples trust an LLM-generated summary containing verification/authorization assertions.
data.correction: Use an explicitly selected SIP participant's documented attributes or a trusted application binding; room metadata has no inherent phone-number contract. Treat number matching as enrichment, keep retrieved text separate from trusted policy, and label verification/action claims from authoritative records rather than allowing a summary to establish them.
data.book_implication: A small trust-aware handoff question adds value; preserve SYS-08 and P3-11 rather than teaching that CRM context automatically verifies the caller.

data.finding: Course uses AgentTest, say(), tool_was_called and list-style session.run rather than the inspected SDK surface. It also calls the harness network-free while teaching an LLM judge.
data.correction: Use pinned AgentSession.run(user_input=...), RunResult assertions and the actual mock_tools helper. Label scripted, model-backed and real-audio lanes separately.

mock_tools is a helper with context-manager or session-scoped behavior

data.finding: The strategy lesson discourages evaluation gates but later lessons gate deployment on regression evaluation. Example thresholds, repeat counts, sample percentages and cohort sizes are heuristics.
data.correction: Define separately hard safety gates, calibrated quality criteria and exploratory scores; freeze corpus/rubric/judge versions, sample design and uncertainty before comparisons.

data.finding: Course examples use agent.toml, lk agent secret set/list and unverified Cloud scaling files; sibling lessons disagree about configurable scaling. A major/minor image tag is also mutable.
data.correction: Use current livekit.toml and the current CLI/secret command reference, keep platform-managed scaling separate from self-hosted HPA proposals, and pin an immutable image digest for reproducibility.

data.topic: Metric types, lifecycle and business truth
data.finding: Custom-metrics code iterates event.metrics, treats generation duration as end-to-end turn latency and uses Agent.on_close. The pinned event contains one AgentMetrics value; that event is deprecated, with usage and per-message latency surfaces identified explicitly.
data.correction: Observe actual typed session/report events, choose a measured start/end, and count bookings from committed business receipts rather than an agent-local boolean. Preserve bounded labels and privacy.

Agent enter and exit hooks are explicit

data.finding: Lessons assert default metrics at 7880 without configuration, worker registration through Redis and all room state in Redis/stateless server. These claims collapse media, cluster routing and agent registration.
data.correction: Configure and verify the metrics endpoint; agent servers register via WebSocket. Redis-backed routing does not serialize active WebRTC/media/process state or P1 business receipts.

data.topic: Scope of operational and product claims
data.finding: Cloud-only/physically-impossible feature wording, compliance shortcuts, transparent failover, instant rollback and unconditional zero-downtime language exceed the cited configuration and fault model. A grace period is a bound, not a guarantee every session ends in time.
data.correction: Verify current feature availability and contract terms independently. Describe bounded routing/drain/restore behavior, tested failure modes and explicit fallback policy; do not infer compliance from provider or hosting choice.

data.finding: Course hook has one argument and invented context fields/default-hook forwarding; the pgvector example performs synchronous cursor work inside async search. RAG/citations are also described too strongly as a fix for hallucination.
data.correction: Use the pinned two-argument hook and ChatContext operations; bound nonblocking I/O, source/context sizes and real ownership. Treat retrieved prose as evidence, require support checks and an abstention path.

evidence.claim: Hook receives ChatContext and a new ChatMessage; default implementation is pass

data.finding: The Python and TypeScript SemanticCache examples key normalized query hashes. Python stores an embedding and threshold but never compares them. TTL alone neither bounds memory nor enforces tenant/ACL/document-version validity.
data.correction: Call that an exact normalized cache, or implement and evaluate real semantic matching. Bound entries/bytes and bind authorization, document/index/model/prompt/voice dependencies as appropriate; invalidate on evidence changes.

evidence.claim: get derives SHA-256 normalized query key; query_embedding and threshold are not used to search.

data.finding: The course names LangChainLLM and a TypeScript plugin without establishing compatibility. Its timeout wrapper is labeled a hard limit, and saver construction/checkpoint identity need lifecycle and scope review.
data.correction: Current official LiveKit guide documents Python LLMAdapter(graph=...). Manage the selected saver correctly, preserve real in-flight work and keep graph memory distinct from accepted-work/consent/effect authority.

data.finding: Course imports livekit.plugins.mcp.MCPToolProvider and supplies tools to AgentSession; that is not the inspected pinned MCP surface. Model-visible descriptions cannot establish caller identity or exact human confirmation.
data.correction: Use verified MCPServer implementations through mcp_servers in the pinned core and enforce authorization/idempotency at application boundaries. Do not treat tool discovery as durable business orchestration.

data.finding: Fixed retrieval budgets, worker capacities, WER/MOS rankings, prices and stack latency numbers lack a reproducible common workload. Claims that all partial STT immediately drives committed LLM output ignore configured turn handling.
data.correction: Use dated capability/pricing sources and a frozen representative corpus; define measurement boundaries, model versions, language/noise conditions, retries and errors. Keep speculative generation and durable acceptance distinct.

evidence.claim: Audio duration is in seconds, distinct from wall duration
Character billing and token billing are separate TTS quantities

data.finding: Room prefixes, phone numbers, metadata, model citations and a prompt telling the model to verify identity are not independent application authorization. Raw query/error logging and unscoped reuse can disclose private context.
data.correction: Derive scope from authenticated trusted bindings, authorize each source/result disclosure, and keep exact action confirmation at the existing authority. Scope persistent thread/cache keys and protect evaluation traces.

data.finding: The public pages show a first multiple-choice item and a 1-of-5 counter. Issuer endorsement, assessment integrity and credential recognition were not independently verified; footer branding is insufficient.
data.correction: Use these as study prompts only. Do not claim an official LiveKit credential, exam completion or full question-bank review. Advertised 120 minutes differs from the 160-minute sum, a planning metadata issue.
